hook_text: One learner got 2 heads in 10. Another got 9. The board said 150 in 300.
clip_script:
A Grade 8 class is told that a fair coin lands heads half the time, and a learner at the back says that is not what happens in real life, because he once got five tails in a row. The teacher hands out thirty coins and says: ten tosses each, write your heads on the board.

The board fills with thirty small numbers, mostly fours, fives and sixes. One learner got 2 heads in ten, another got 9. The individual results are all over the place. Then the teacher adds the column: 150 heads out of 300 tosses. Relative frequency 0,5. One learner's ten tosses are a story. Thirty learners' three hundred tosses are evidence. The probability was right all along; it just needed enough trials to show itself.
visual_style: A chalkboard column of scattered small numbers; a wobbly relative-frequency line swings wildly then narrows onto a steady 0,5 as a counter climbs to 300
call_to_action: Open the full session to run the trials and see relative frequency meet probability.
